newsitem.title: CANADA: Bell Canada seeks live broadcast tests.
newsitem.headline: Bell Canada seeks live broadcast tests.

text.p: BCE Inc's Bell Canada unit began testifying on Monday before the federal broadcast regulator CRTC in support of its bid to conduct a two-year experimental broadcast distribution license.

Bell told the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission that its two-year market trial would let it create two "living labs" in London, Ontario and Repentigny, Quebec, venturing into high-tech communications.
"The convergence of broadcasting, computing and telephony presents new opportunities and new challenges for broadcasters and content providers," Bell Vice President John Sullivan said.

"Bell is venturing into an area in which it is has very limited experience and it has a lot to learn about broadcasting -- from how to integrate digital systems to the packaging of content," Sullivan said.
"We need to discover how to do things in new ways, such as how to use the huge bandwidth available to deliver interactivity and services like near video on demand."

Among the features of the trial, Bell plans to package broadcast services with telecommunications services such as high-speed computer access, granting Internet access at a much faster rate than currently available.
Bell's rivals oppose the trial, saying it will convince those participating in the experiment to stay with Bell.
If approved, Bell would begin the trial in June at a cost of about C$80 million.
